hints: Because numerator and denominator have the same degree, first identify the constant polynomial term $A$.
Compare coefficients of $x^3,x^2,x,$ and the constant term to determine $B,C,D$.
Recombine the terms briefly to check the decomposition.
walkthrough:
Observe that the numerator $3x^3 + 6x - 8$ and denominator $x(x^2 + 2) = x^3 + 2x$ both have degree $3$. Dividing the leading terms gives the constant term $A$:
$$A = \dfrac{3x^3}{x^3} = 3$$

Set up the partial fraction decomposition identity:
$$\dfrac{3x^3 + 6x - 8}{x(x^2 + 2)} = 3 + \dfrac{B}{x} + \dfrac{Cx + D}{x^2 + 2}$$

Multiply through by the common denominator $x(x^2 + 2)$:
$$3x^3 + 6x - 8 = 3x(x^2 + 2) + B(x^2 + 2) + (Cx + D)x$$

Expand the right-hand side and collect terms by powers of $x$:
$$3x^3 + 6x - 8 = 3x^3 + 6x + Bx^2 + 2B + Cx^2 + Dx$$
$$3x^3 + 6x - 8 = 3x^3 + (B + C)x^2 + (6 + D)x + 2B$$

Subtract $3x^3 + 6x$ from both sides:
$$-8 = (B + C)x^2 + Dx + 2B$$

Equate coefficients on both sides:
Constant term: $2B = -8 \implies B = -4$
Coefficient of $x$: $D = 0$
Coefficient of $x^2$: $B + C = 0 \implies C = -B = -(-4) = 4$

State the complete partial fraction expansion of $f(x)$:
$$f(x) = 3 - \dfrac{4}{x} + \dfrac{4x}{x^2 + 2}$$

ai_rubric.Partial Fractions: Identifies or derives $A=3$; Derives one of $B=-4$, $C=4$ and $D=0$; Concludes with $f(x)=3-\frac4x+\frac{4x}{x^2+2}$.

hints: Recognise $4x/(x^2+2)$ as a constant multiple of the derivative of $x^2+2$ over itself.
Apply the bounds 1 and 2 to $3x-4\ln x+2\ln(x^2+2)$.
Use logarithm laws to simplify the exact result to the required form.
walkthrough:
Use the partial fractions from part (i) to set up the definite integral:
$$\int_1^2 f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x = \int_1^2 \left(3 - \dfrac{4}{x} + \dfrac{4x}{x^2 + 2}\right)\mathrm{d}x$$

Integrate each term individually:
$$\int 3\,\mathrm{d}x = 3x$$
$$\int -\dfrac{4}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x = -4\ln x \quad (\text{since } x > 0 \text{ on } [1, 2])$$
$$\int \dfrac{4x}{x^2 + 2}\,\mathrm{d}x = 2\int \dfrac{2x}{x^2 + 2}\,\mathrm{d}x = 2\ln(x^2 + 2)$$

Combine into the integrated expression:
$$\int_1^2 f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x = \left[3x - 4\ln x + 2\ln(x^2 + 2)\right]_1^2$$

Subtract the lower limit evaluation from the upper limit evaluation:
$$\int_1^2 f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x = (6 - 4\ln 2 + 2\ln 6) - (3 + 2\ln 3) = (6 - 3) - 4\ln 2 + 2(\ln 6 - \ln 3)$$

Simplify using the quotient law of logarithms $\ln 6 - \ln 3 = \ln\left(\dfrac{6}{3}\right) = \ln 2$:
$$\int_1^2 f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x = 3 - 4\ln 2 + 2\ln 2 = 3 - 2\ln 2$$

Apply the power law of logarithms $2\ln 2 = \ln(2^2) = \ln 4$ to obtain the required exact form:
$$\int_1^2 f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x = 3 - \ln 4$$

ai_rubric.Integration: Integrates and derives $3x-4\ln x$; Derives term $2\ln(x^2+2)$; Concludes with $\int_1^2f(x)\,dx=3-\ln4$.
